notes: THE ESCALATION. What determines the rendered bytes of canvas.2d and webgl.readpixels, in descending order of effect. (1) The ANGLE backend. It fixes the shader translator output, the rasterisation rules, and the whole limit/precision/extension table. Selectable at runtime with --use-angle, but bounded by the host OS: Metal exists only on Apple, D3D11 only on Windows. (2) The GPU driver underneath ANGLE. Not configurable. This is the irreducible residue. (3) The driver-bug workaround set - 142 workarounds, 253 list entries, all keyed on GPUInfo fields we are already spoofing, each forceable by switch. This is Chromium's own mechanism for making rendering differ deterministically per device, and it is already shipping. (4) MSAA sample count and resolve mode (webgl.antialias-samples). (5) Canvas 2D raster mode, GPU or CPU, via --disable-accelerated-2d-canvas and the readback fallback. (6) --disable-2d-canvas-antialiasing and --disable-2d-canvas-clip-antialiasing. (7) Text rasterisation: SkFont edging, hinting and subpixel positioning, plus the eight RendererPreferences font-render-params fields on Linux. (8) The installed font set (owned by subsystem 7). (9) The image encoder, which is constant. RECOMMENDATION. Items 3 to 7 are all existing, deterministic, per-process configuration and should be driven from the profile; none requires per-pixel interference and none violates A3. Item 1 is the hard constraint and it forces a structural decision: profiles must be partitioned by OS and ANGLE backend, and a profile may only be loaded on a host that can provide its backend. A macOS/Metal profile on a Linux host is not a patching problem, it is an impossible claim - webgpu.preferred-canvas-format alone gives it away in one property read before any render is compared. The concrete first step is to set GPUInfo to the profile's device before gpu::ComputeGpuFeatureInfo runs, so that the blocklist, the workaround set, the disabled-extension set and the MSAA count all follow the claimed device using Chromium's own tables rather than the host's hardware. WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED, and what would settle it: how large the residual difference is between two GPUs on the same OS and backend. The ANGLE caps table says the reported limits do not differ at all; it says nothing about the pixels. We need two T0 captures on the same OS and ANGLE backend but different GPU models - say an M1 MacBook and this M4 Max - and a diff of probes['canvas.2d'].pixels_sha256 and probes['webgl1'].pixels_sha256. observable: (await navigator.storage.estimate()).quota
verdict_reason: The reported quota is no longer a function of disk space. With storage::features::kStaticStorageQuota enabled by default, CalculateReportedQuota returns usage + 10 GiB for every profile whose partition volume has at least 10 GiB of TOTAL space, which is every plausible reference device. The host value is therefore already exactly the reference value - a constant 10737418240 for a fresh origin - and carries no host information to spoof. The residual risk is a container or VM with a volume smaller than 10 GiB, where the answer becomes ceil(total/1GiB)*1GiB and does leak the host; that is a deployment constraint recorded as coh.reported-quota-is-static-not-disk, not a value to patch.

evidence.note: CalculateReportedQuota: `if (clamped_total_space_bytes >= 10 * QuotaManagerImpl::kGBytes) return clamped_usage_bytes + 10 * kGBytes;` otherwise usage + ceil(total/1GiB)*1GiB. kGBytes = 1024^3 at quota_manager_impl.h:161

BASE_FEATURE(kStaticStorageQuota, base::FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT) - the in-tree comment calls it 'a kill switch for the new reported quota being a static value', so static is the shipping behaviour and dynamic is the fallback

navigator.storage.estimate() reaches GetUsageAndReportedQuotaWithBreakdown, not GetUsageAndQuotaWithBreakdown; GetUsageAndQuotaForDevtools (quota_manager_impl.cc:1224) keeps the unfiltered path, so DevTools and the page disagree in stock Chrome

the disk-derived path that no longer reaches JS: pool_size = total * kPoolSizeRatio (0.8, quota_features.cc:26) and per_storage_key_quota = pool_size * 0.75, still enforced for writes but not reported
Chromium's own expectation, in a browser test: 'Reported quota is the lower of 10 GiB or disk size rounded up to the nearest 1 GiB', computed as min(10, (disk_size - 1)/kGiB + 1)
quota 10737418240 (exactly 10 * 2^30), usage 0, usageDetails {} on a real headed Chrome 152 on an M4 Max - the constant, not a disk-derived number

notes: This row corrects a widely held assumption. Every anti-detect writeup that treats navigator.storage.estimate().quota as 'about 60% of free disk' is describing pre-M110 Chrome; at 152 the free-space term is gone entirely and even total space only matters below 10 GiB. The practical consequences are the reverse of the usual advice: (1) there is nothing to spoof here and a tool that writes a plausible disk-derived number into quota produces a value stock Chrome cannot emit; (2) the only way to get a wrong answer is to run in incognito or on a tiny volume; (3) quota is usage-additive, so a site that has written 100 MB legitimately sees 10 GiB + 100 MB and a fixed 10 GiB response to every caller is itself the anomaly. The V3 check is an equality against 10737418240 + usage rather than a range.

observable: navigator.permissions.query({name: N}).state for every queryable N, read as a whole map
verdict_reason: The default state map is a pure function of Chromium's content-settings registry and a handful of permission contexts that override it, all compile-time constants. It is identical on every fresh headed profile on every desktop platform, and the capture reproduces it exactly. There is no host input to spoof. What the map does require is negative: the browser must not be built on or launched as chrome-headless-shell, and the profile must not carry pre-seeded content settings, because either flips values the reference device does not flip.

evidence.note: measured on real headed Chrome 152 / macOS: geolocation prompt, notifications prompt, camera prompt, microphone prompt, midi prompt, background-sync GRANTED, persistent-storage prompt, clipboard-read prompt, clipboard-write GRANTED, accelerometer GRANTED, gyroscope GRANTED, magnetometer GRANTED, screen-wake-lock GRANTED, payment-handler GRANTED. Seven granted, seven prompt, none denied

accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer all fall through to CreatePermissionDescriptor(PermissionName::SENSORS), so the three names read one bit and must always be equal

HeadlessPermissionManager::GetPermissionStatus returns ASK for every permission unconditionally, so in chrome-headless-shell all seven granted names read 'prompt' - a seven-name divergence from headed Chrome, not the single Notification tell it is usually reduced to

notes: This answers the question the shard was asked: a real headed Chrome, fresh profile, secure top-level context, reports exactly seven granted (background-sync, clipboard-write, accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, screen-wake-lock, payment-handler) and prompt for everything else; nothing defaults to denied. None of these change under automation - --enable-automation, the CDP attach and the PermissionRequestManager auto-dismiss behaviour all affect permission *requests*, never the queried state. The only default-state divergence found anywhere in the tree is the old headless binary, and it moves seven names at once. If it never does, this row closes as out-of-scope with that as the reason and nothing is patched. If it does, the incognito quota path is a double failure - it flags the profile as incognito on any machine with under roughly 60 GiB of RAM, and the number it reports leaks host physical memory to within about 30%, which then has to agree with navigator.deviceMemory's bucketed claim. It also re-randomises per launch, so the same profile returns a different quota on Tuesday than on Monday, which breaks returning-visitor consistency and violates axiom A3 even though the randomness is Chromium's own. What would settle it: (1) a statement of whether incognito profiles are in scope; and if they are, (2) a T0 capture from a real headed Chrome incognito window on known hardware to confirm the derived arithmetic, and (3) a decision between enabling storage::features::kIncognitoStaticStorageQuota - Chromium's own already-written fix, one line in the feature list - and patching CalculateIncognitoDynamicSettings. observable: await navigator.getBattery() then {charging, level, chargingTime, dischargingTime}

evidence.note: charging true, level 0.24, chargingTime 5160, dischargingTime null (Infinity through JSON) on a real charging MacBook

evidence.source: the same probe across the four captures in resources/fingerprints/raw/
evidence.note: varies between sessions on one machine, which is why docs/METHODOLOGY.md treats it as device state rather than identity - unlike speech.voices, which did not move

level is current_capacity / max_capacity, a raw unrounded double with no bucketing anywhere in Chromium; chargingTime and dischargingTime are base::Minutes(k).InSeconds() and are therefore always exact multiples of 60, or Infinity when unknown. 5160 is 86 minutes

the struct defaults are charging true, charging_time 0, discharging_time INFINITY, level 1; any platform with no BatteryStatusManager - battery_status_manager_default.cc:38, or Linux where UPower reports no battery - never overwrites them, so getBattery() resolves that exact tuple

notes: Escalated because the honest answer depends on a decision this shard cannot make. The values themselves are device state and inheriting them is right on a host with a real battery, which is what the M4 Max capture shows. The problem is the other host: a datacentre VM has no battery, so getBattery() resolves the mojom defaults exactly - {charging: true, level: 1, chargingTime: 0, dischargingTime: Infinity} - and that tuple contradicts a profile claiming a MacBook. What makes this an escalation rather than a patch is that the same tuple is perfectly correct for a real iMac, Mac Studio, Mac mini or desktop PC, so the cheap fix is a profile constraint - desktop profiles on battery-less hosts, laptop profiles only on hosts with batteries - and no code at all. What would settle it: a ruling on whether laptop profiles must be servable from battery-less hosts. If they must, this becomes a hard problem rather than a value to set, because axiom A3 forbids per-call randomness while a battery that reads 0.24 for an hour and then 0.24 again tomorrow is itself the tell; a synthesised battery needs a monotonic, wall-clock-driven discharge model with the chargingTime/dischargingTime multiple-of-60 invariant preserved, and that is a design task deserving its own row. Note also the derived constraints a detector can check for free: exactly one of chargingTime and dischargingTime is finite, and the finite one is always a multiple of 60.

when RuntimeEnabledFeatures::WebAudioRustFftEnabled() the constructor allocates rust_fft_ = blink::rust_fft::rustfft_new(fft_size_) and DoFFT/DoInverseFFT route to RustFFT, bypassing PlatformDoFFT entirely. WebAudioRustFft is status:"stable" at runtime_enabled_features.json5:6979-6980, so this is the default path in a stable 152 build.

THE CPU DEPENDENCE. FftPlanner::new() selects, at runtime, FftPlannerAvx -> FftPlannerSse -> FftPlannerNeon -> FftPlannerWasmSimd -> FftPlannerScalar. avx_planner.rs:124-126 requires is_x86_feature_detected!("avx") && is_x86_feature_detected!("fma"). third_party/rust/rustfft/v6/BUILD.gn:91-95 enables the avx, sse and neon features, so all four kernels are compiled in and the choice is made by the host CPU.

the kernels are not arithmetically equivalent. AVX uses fmadd/fmaddsub (one rounding), NEON uses vfmaq_f32 (one rounding), SSE uses _mm_add_ps(acc, _mm_mul_ps(a, b)) (two roundings). Same input, different float32 output. -ffp-contract=off does not touch explicit FMA intrinsics.

a second, independent architecture split: OscillatorHandler::ProcessKRateVector and ProcessARateVectorKernel have three separate bodies - SSE2 on x86/x64, NEON on arm/arm64, and a scalar fallback at oscillator_handler.cc:357 and :368 for everything else. The SSE2 file documents the divergence in its own comment at :115-117 ("Ideally, to preserve accuracy, we should use (two) packed double vectors for this, but that degrades performance quite a bit") and again at :188 ("There's a bit of round-off above").

THE OS DEPENDENCE. Both calls are UNQUALIFIED - sin(static_cast<double>(kPiOverTwoFloat * compressor_gain)) in the per-sample gain warp, and exp(...) in KneeCurve - so they bind to the host libm from <cmath>, not to fdlibm. The same file uses fdlibm::powf at :145 and fdlibm::asinf at :190, so this is an inconsistency in Chromium rather than a deliberate choice.

DecibelsToLinear returns powf(10, 0.05f*decibels) and LinearToDecibels returns 20*log10f(linear) - both unqualified host-libm float functions, in a file that includes fdlibm/ieee754.h and uses fdlibm::exp at :69. These are on the compressor's per-sample metering path (dynamics_compressor.cc:337) and inside Saturate/KneeCurve, so a 1-ULP libm difference feeds metering_gain_ -> db_compression_diff -> envelope_rate -> compressor_gain -> the output samples.

-ffp-contract=off is applied unconditionally under is_clang, so the COMPILER never fuses a*b+c on its own. This rules out compiler-introduced FMA divergence and leaves exactly two mechanisms: explicit FMA intrinsics inside rustfft/NEON, and the host libm.

vector_math picks its backend at COMPILE time - mac (Accelerate vDSP) / neon / x86 / scalar. Vsmul and Vmaxmgv, the two operations CreateBandLimitedTables uses, are exactly-rounded per element in every backend, so this split does not by itself change the render. cpu/x86/vector_math_x86.h:29-30 adds a RUNTIME base::CPU().has_avx() dispatch which does matter for the order-dependent reductions used elsewhere in the graph.

the pre-RustFFT backends are still compiled in and still OS-split - Accelerate vDSP on Mac (vDSP_fft_zrip at fft_frame_mac.cc:138,154), PFFFT everywhere else, guarded by #if !BUILDFLAG(IS_MAC). Disabling WebAudioRustFft therefore changes the render wholesale and deterministically. It is a Chromium-version lever, not a device lever.

evidence.source: resources/surfaces.json, category audio: "DynamicsCompressorNode - its quirky DSP behaviour across CPU/OS combinations is the entropy source"
evidence.note: the field's own folk model, recorded because it turns out to be right for the wrong reason: the entropy is libm plus ISA dispatch, not anything peculiar to the compressor's design

notes: THE ESCALATION, and the answer to what determines the rendered float samples. It is NOT the audio hardware. Nothing in the offline path reads a device: sample rate, length and channel count are constructor arguments (offline_audio_context.cc:98), MaxChannelCount is the constructor value (offline_audio_destination_handler.cc:95), and the render quantum is a fixed 128. Two machines with different sound cards, different sample rates and no audio device at all render identical bytes. So this surface carries no information about the claimed device and cannot be made to. What it DOES identify, in descending order of effect: (1) THE HOST CPU'S INSTRUCTION SET, at runtime. rustfft's FftPlanner::new() picks AVX+FMA, SSE, NEON or scalar by CPU feature detection, and those kernels are not arithmetically equivalent - AVX and NEON fuse the multiply-add, SSE does not. The oscillator's entire wave table is inverse-FFT output, so every sample inherits this. An x86 host without FMA and an x86 host with it produce different hashes from the same binary. (2) THE HOST OS, through libm. dynamics_compressor.cc:331 and :477 and audio_utilities.cc:38,:44 call sin, exp, powf and log10f unqualified, so Apple libm, glibc and UCRT each give their own last-ULP answers, and the compressor's feedback loop amplifies them rather than damping them. (3) THE TARGET ARCHITECTURE THE BINARY WAS BUILT FOR, through the three hand-written oscillator kernels (SSE2 / NEON / scalar) whose own comments admit they differ in round-off. (4) THE CHROMIUM BUILD CONFIGURATION - WebAudioRustFft on or off swaps RustFFT for vDSP-on-Mac or PFFFT-elsewhere. This is the audio analogue of the ANGLE finding in gpu.angle-backend, and it is worse in one respect: ANGLE at least hard-codes a table that is stable per backend, whereas here the arithmetic itself is selected by CPUID at process start. RECOMMENDATION. Treat the audio render exactly as the GPU shard treats the ANGLE backend: partition the profile set by (os-family, cpu-isa-class) and refuse to load a profile whose partition the host cannot provide. A macOS/arm64 profile is renderable only on an arm64 Mac; an x86 profile captured on an AVX2 machine is not reproducible on a pre-AVX host. Do not attempt to reconcile the difference in code. Explicitly rejected: per-call noise (A3, and the cloakbrowser capture above measures it as 1-4 ULP on 71% of samples on identical hardware - a corpus diff catches it in one probe); intercepting getChannelData or startRendering (A1); and replaying corpus samples, which cannot work because a detector chooses the graph. The one legitimate deterministic lever is the WebAudioRustFft RuntimeEnabledFeature, and it selects a Chromium version's arithmetic, not a device's. WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED, and what would settle it: we hold exactly one T0 audio render, from one (macOS, arm64, RustFFT) host. We do not know the SIZE of the partitions. Needed: the same probe captured on (a) an Intel Mac - Apple libm with x86+AVX+FMA, (b) a Linux x86 host with AVX+FMA, (c) a Linux x86 host with AVX masked off so the SSE planner is taken, (d) an arm64 Linux or Android device, and (e) a second arm64 Mac of a different model. Diffing full_sha256 across (a)-(d) separates the libm term from the ISA term; (e) confirms that CPU model within an ISA class does not matter. Until those exist the partition boundaries are inference, not measurement.

observable: RTCIceCandidate.priority and .foundation, and the 'network-id' and 'network-cost' extension fields inside the raw RTCIceCandidate.candidate string

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE WIRE FORM. Candidate::ToString appends ' network-id <id>' whenever network_id() > 0 and ' network-cost <cost>' whenever network_cost() > 0, directly into the a=candidate line that JavaScript reads from RTCIceCandidate.candidate. Neither is redacted by anything.

THE HOLE IN mDNS. Candidate::ToSanitizedCopy rewrites only address, related_address and optionally username. priority, foundation, network_id and network_cost survive obfuscation untouched, so a candidate whose address is a random .local hostname still states which interface it came from and how that interface ranks.
MergeNetworkList sorts the interfaces and then assigns preference 127, 126, 125 ... in order. So the local-preference byte of every candidate's priority is (127 - rank of its interface).

priority = (type_pref << 24) | (((network_adapter_preference << 8) | IPAddressPrecedence(addr)) + relay_pref) << 8 | (256 - component). The interface rank is therefore recoverable from the priority of any candidate by arithmetic, and the count of distinct ranks is the number of interfaces.

network-cost is a direct readout of the ADAPTER TYPE: 0 ethernet/loopback, 10 wifi, 50 unknown, 250/500/910/980 for 5G/4G/3G/2G cellular, 999 for a type the manager deliberately refuses to name, +1 if the interface is a VPN. A single integer in the SDP says whether the machine is on ethernet, wifi, cellular or VPN.

The adapter type is derived in the renderer from net::NetworkInterface::type, falling back to webrtc::GetAdapterTypeFromName(it->name) - string matching on the real interface name - and is forced to ADAPTER_TYPE_VPN when IsVpnMacAddress(*it->mac_address) matches, i.e. from the host MAC's OUI.
net->set_id(next_available_network_id_++) - network-id is a small sequential integer, so the highest network-id seen is a lower bound on how many interfaces the host has ever had during the session.

notes: NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS PROJECT, and it is the reason mDNS is not a solution. A detector that never learns a single IP address can still read, from an offer SDP alone: how many network interfaces the machine has, how they rank against each other, whether each is ethernet / wifi / cellular / VPN, and - by the VPN bit at ipc_network_manager.cc:130 - whether a VPN adapter with a recognised MAC prefix is present. A machine that reports one wifi interface, or three interfaces of which one is flagged VPN, has described itself precisely. The fix is the same single patch as webrtc.ice-candidates and that is the argument for placing it in the network service: replacing the interface list there sets the count, the order, the types and hence every one of these fields consistently. Replacing them anywhere downstream means reproducing MergeNetworkList's sort by hand and getting the same answer, which is strictly harder and easy to get subtly wrong. Coherence obligation with subsystem 3: if the profile claims a laptop the interface set should look like a laptop's, and network-cost 0 on every interface (all-ethernet) on a machine whose profile claims a MacBook is an internal contradiction.

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH. THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS LEVER. When a range IS configured, the loop is `for (port = min_port; port <= max_port && result < 0; ++port)` - it binds the LOWEST FREE PORT, ascending, deterministically. Setting --webrtc-udp-port-range to a plausible macOS range would therefore produce candidates on 49152, 49153, 49154 ... which is a far louder signal than an out-of-range port, because no kernel allocates ephemeral ports that way.

Marked T3 deliberately - these are widely known defaults but we have measured none of them ourselves, and net_preferred_port_range is host-configurable. The magnitude of the signal is unknown until measured.

observable: The a=fingerprint line of a createOffer SDP - the hash algorithm token - and the expires value of a certificate obtained from RTCPeerConnection.generateCertificate()
verdict_reason: The certificate is generated fresh per RTCPeerConnection from KT_DEFAULT = KT_ECDSA on curve EC_NIST_P256, with a fixed 30-day lifetime and a fixed one-day backdated window. The fingerprint bytes are therefore random per connection and carry no host entropy, and the algorithm, curve and lifetime are libwebrtc constants that depend only on the revision. Nothing about the machine reaches this value.

evidence.note: enum KeyType { KT_RSA, KT_ECDSA, KT_LAST, KT_DEFAULT = KT_ECDSA }; KeyParams(KT_DEFAULT) selects params_.curve = EC_NIST_P256.

KeyParams key_params = KeyParams(); then GenerateCertificateAsync - the default-constructed KeyParams is the only one used when the application supplies no certificate, which is the case for every ordinary RTCPeerConnection.

kDefaultCertificateLifetimeInSeconds = 30 days and kCertificateWindowInSeconds = -1 day, so generateCertificate().expires is deterministically now + 30 days and is a clock readout rather than a device readout.

notes: Resolved as inherit on T1. observable: MediaDeviceInfo.deviceId for each entry of navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices() - its format, its stability across repeated calls, across reloads and across sessions, and its value before any capture permission is granted
verdict_reason: The emitted value is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the requesting origin over (raw device id || per-storage-key salt), hex-encoded lowercase. It is a 64-character string with no host-derived structure, it differs per origin, and it is uncorrelated with the underlying hardware. There is nothing in the value to make correct that is not already correct. What must be true is a property of the raw device list rather than of this transform, and that belongs to media.device-counts.

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH. GetHMACForRawMediaDeviceID: key = origin.Serialize(); hmac over raw_device_id then over device_id_salt (or group_id_salt); base::HexEncodeLower of the 32-byte SHA-256 result. Empty ids and the literals 'default' and 'communications' short-circuit and are returned VERBATIM - see media.audio-output-special-ids.

TranslateMediaDeviceInfo: without permission it returns WebMediaDeviceInfo(std::string(), std::string(), std::string(), ...) - empty deviceId, empty label AND empty groupId. This is the browser-process source of the hasLabels:false we measured.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE AUDIO SHARD. `if (!has_permissions[i] && !translation[i].empty()) break;` - without permission the loop emits exactly ONE entry per device kind regardless of how many devices exist. The same truncation is written a second time at media_devices_util.cc:191-193.

Read together with the truncation above, this capture establishes only that the M4 Max has at least one device of each kind. It does NOT establish that it has exactly one. The corpus row for pre-permission counts is therefore a constant, not a measurement.

The salt is persistent per storage key via MediaDeviceSaltService if and only if cookie_settings->IsFullCookieAccessAllowed for this frame; otherwise the ephemeral BrowserContext::UniqueId() is used and are_persistent_device_ids_allowed is false.

When persistence is not allowed the per-document frame_salt is appended, and that frame salt is regenerated on every navigation (media_device_id_salt_base_ = CreateRandomMediaDeviceIDSalt()). So deviceId is stable across reloads when cookies are allowed and changes on every navigation when they are not - which makes deviceId stability itself a readout of the cookie setting for that site.

notes: Resolved as inherit, and it EXTENDS media.device-counts rather than restating it. Three things fall out that the audio shard could not see from the counts alone. (1) The pre-permission shape is a constant: one entry per kind with three empty strings. Any profile whose spoofed device list is applied at the audio-service end automatically reproduces it, and any implementation that instead fabricates deviceIds in the renderer will emit non-empty ids without permission, which is a decisive tell. (2) Once permission IS granted the full list appears with real HMACs, so the count that matters for V3 is the post-permission one and the corpus currently holds only the pre-permission one - the collector should gain a permission-granted variant of the media.devices probe, run under --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream, to capture it. (3) Because the transform is deterministic in the raw id, the raw ids the patched device list supplies must be STABLE for the life of the profile: a raw id regenerated per call would make deviceId change between two enumerateDevices() calls in one document, which axiom A3 forbids and no real device does.

observable: MediaDeviceInfo.groupId across kinds - whether a camera and a microphone share a groupId, whether groupId is stable across reloads, and whether it equals any deviceId
verdict_reason: groupId is the same HMAC transform as deviceId over the raw group id, differing only in which salt is mixed in, so the emitted string carries no host-derived structure either. What it encodes is a relation - which devices are physically the same unit - and that relation is a property of the raw device list produced by the audio and video capture services, not of this code. It is correct once the device list is correct.

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE ASYMMETRY. group_id_salt = StrCat({salt, frame_salt, "group_id"}) - the per-document frame_salt is mixed in UNCONDITIONALLY, whereas device_id_salt appends it only when persistent ids are disallowed. The comment states the intent: 'must be unique per document, but it must also change if cookies are cleared'.
An empty raw group_id is passed through as an empty string rather than hashed, so a device whose backend supplies no group id is distinguishable from one that does.

Video group ids are back-filled from a heuristic that matches camera names against audio device group ids - which is why MediaDevicesDispatcherHost::OnVideoGotSaltAndOrigin at :399-402 requests audio devices even when only video was asked for. The camera-microphone grouping on a laptop is manufactured by that heuristic, not read from hardware.

notes: Left open rather than resolved because it states a requirement on the spoofed device list that nothing else in the ledger states, and we cannot check it without a permission-granted capture. On a real laptop the built-in camera and the built-in microphone share a groupId, produced by the name-matching heuristic above; a spoofed device list that gives them independent raw group ids produces a machine whose webcam and mic are separate USB peripherals, which contradicts a claimed MacBook. Conversely a spoofed list whose group ids are all identical claims every device is one physical unit. The correct behaviour is to carry raw group ids in the profile alongside the raw device ids and let the existing HMAC do the rest. Also worth recording as a live detection: because groupId is salted per document and deviceId is not (when cookies are allowed), a page can compare the two across a reload and learn its own cookie-permission state - stock behaviour, but a fork that made deviceId per-document to look 'safer' would break the asymmetry and be detectable by exactly that comparison.

ARBITER NOTE ON THE PROFILE SCHEMA: this row names profile_field media.devices, which is deliberately not the media.device_counts field the audio shard's media.device-counts row names. Counts alone cannot express 'a device whose raw id is the literal string communications', and neither can they express the raw group id relations that media.device-group-ids needs. The recommendation is that media.device_counts be generalised into a media.devices list of {kind, raw_device_id, raw_group_id, label} entries, from which the counts are derived rather than stated; the two rows then draw on one field instead of two that can disagree.
